details: The query transcript identifying a fixed target is a teaching set for that target.
proof: Fix a target $h$ and run any membership-query learner that identifies it.  The coordinates queried on the path leading to $h$ must distinguish $h$ from every other concept; otherwise that concept gives the same transcript and the learner cannot identify the target.  Thus they form a teaching set for $h$, of size at most $\mathrm{Q}_m(\mathcal{H})$.  Maximizing over $h$ yields $\mathrm{RHT}(\mathcal{H})\le\mathrm{Q}_m(\mathcal{H})$.
witness_verification: For $n$ singleton concepts, membership-query complexity is $n-1$, while relative hitting size is 1.
name: Membership Query Complexity / Relative Hitting Size
